subject: DPA — Training use carve-out and EU transfer (Finovate Bank)

Subject: DPA redline + proposed carve-out for model training

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is our current DPA with a light redline (Redlined_DPA_Finovate_v1.docx). I wanted to surface one specific ask from your legal team around use of Customer Data for model training / product improvement so we’re aligned before broader redlines.

High-level position: Redwood’s hosted inference platform processes customer data to fulfill requests and provide the service. We do not intend to use raw customer content as ongoing supervised training data for base model retraining. We do, however, rely on aggregated telemetry and anonymous usage signals to monitor quality and performance.

Can you confirm whether Finovate needs an explicit statutory "no-training" carve-out (i.e., no use of customer content for model training), or whether a narrower formulation that permits aggregated/anonymous metrics suffices? If you need a proposed clause tracked into the DPA, see the suggested language below:

"No Training on Customer Content: Redwood shall not use Customer Content to improve, train, or fine-tune models that would reproduce, regenerate, or derive Customer Content or Customer Confidential Information. Redwood may collect and use anonymized, aggregated usage metrics and telemetry data for the purposes of improving service reliability and performance, provided that such data cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Content."

Also, a couple quick clarifications we expect you’ll ask about:
- Subprocessors: we’ll provide the current subprocessor list and will notify you of material changes per the DPA.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood uses SCCs where required and can support EU-data residency options for Dedicated/Private deployments; for hosted, SCCs + standard safeguards are typical.

If you’re good with the proposed wording, I can have Legal (cc’d) insert it and we can route the final DPA via DocuSign.

Cheers,
Grace

Hi Grace —

Thanks for sending this along and for the clear language. Our legal team appreciates the "no raw training" stance; a few notes from us:

1) We need an explicit prohibition on using "Customer Content" for any training or model improvement that could reproduce or reveal customer data. The phrase should be broad enough to cover derivative models and not just direct copying.

2) We are okay with aggregated telemetry for reliability/ops, but that must be clearly anonymized and not reversible.

3) Subprocessors: please confirm whether any of your subprocessors process EU-origin data outside the EU/UK, and whether you can commit to prior notification plus objection rights for new subprocessors that would access Customer Content.

4) Cross-border transfers: for EU-origin data we will want SCCs implemented and a clear description of transfer mechanisms.

If you can get a version of the clause that covers items 1–2 and add the subprocessor notification flow, we'll take it to our in-house counsel. We can do a short call early next week if that helps.

Best,

Grace —

Thanks for the context. Below is the redlined clause I recommend inserting into Section 3 (Use of Customer Data). I kept it narrow but protective, and added a subprocessor notification flow and SCC note for transfers. Please include this as a tracked change in the next doc version.

Proposed clause (redline-ready):
"Use of Customer Content; Training Prohibition. Redwood shall process Customer Content solely to provide the Services and for internal service operations (including system monitoring, debugging, and performance optimization). Except as otherwise expressly agreed in writing, Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or develop models or models' underlying weights, parameters, or datasets in a manner that would reproduce, regenerate, or otherwise reveal Customer Content or Customer Confidential Information (\"Training Prohibition\"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and use aggregated and irreversibly anonymized usage metrics and telemetry for purposes of service reliability, capacity planning, and product analytics, provided that such data cannot reasonably be re-associated with specific Customer Content or persons.

Subprocessors. Redwood shall maintain a current list of subprocessors and shall provide Customer with advance notice of new subprocessors that may access Customer Content. Customer shall have thirty (30) days from notice to object in writing to any new subprocessor; if Customer objects for legitimate privacy/security reasons, the parties shall work in good faith to address the concern (including offering alternative hosting options such as Dedicated or Private deployments where applicable).

Transfers. For personal data transfers from the EEA/UK, Redwood shall implement appropriate safeguards such as the EU/UK Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and will provide documentation upon request. For customers requiring data residency, Redwood can offer Dedicated or Private deployment options under a separate hosting addendum.

I will produce a tracked version (DPA_Redline_v2.docx) with the clause inserted and two narrow, redlined alternatives (stricter \"no-derivative\" language and a slightly looser telemetry carve-out) so Finovate can choose. We can sign off on SCCs and the subprocessor notice flow.

If you want, I can draft a single-paragraph summary for procurement they can circulate internally. Recommend sending the tracked doc + a 20-min sync to avoid back-and-forth.

—Marissa
